plans.label: Raise the school homestead exemption
plans.description: The school homestead exemption rises from $140,000 to $180,000 in 2027; the state pays districts back.

plans.label: Buy down school tax rates
plans.description: Every district's compressed school rate falls 4 cents per $100 in 2027 (about what raising the exemption to $180,000 costs); the state pays districts back. Rentals and businesses get the cut too.

knobs.label: Cut in the school rate (cents per $100)

plans.label: Extend the circuit breaker
plans.description: The 20% yearly limit on appraisal increases for rentals and other non-homestead property up to $5.32 million continues through 2036 instead of ending after 2026.

plans.label: Tighten local revenue limits
plans.description: Cities, counties and districts can raise M&O revenue on existing property at most 2.5% a year without an election, down from 3.5% (as in SB 10, which failed in 2025).

plans.label: Lower the homestead appraisal cap to 5%
plans.description: A homestead's appraised value can rise at most 5% a year, down from 10%.

plans.label: More relief for owners 65 and over
plans.description: The extra school exemption for owners 65+ or disabled rises from $60,000 to $100,000, and every county, city and college must freeze their taxes.

plans.label: Credit for owners with high tax for their income
plans.description: The state pays homestead owners with incomes up to $100,000 the amount of their property tax above 5% of income, up to $1,500 a year.

knobs.label: Tax above this share of income

plans.label: Governor Abbott's five steps
plans.description: Homesteads stop paying school taxes (M&O and debt; the state pays districts back); appraisal increases are capped at 3% a year for all property and properties are reappraised only every five years; local levies on existing property may grow at most the lesser of population plus inflation and 3.5%; and rate increases need two-thirds voter approval (modelled as none passing). Rollback petitions are not modelled. "Empowering Texas Taxpayers: Five Steps", Nov 2025.

knobs.label: Share of rate increases that pass

plans.label: Gina Hinojosa's goal
plans.description: Illustrative: her stated end goal of eliminating residential property taxes, phased out evenly over five years from 2027 and paid by the state. She has not said how or when; her near-term step is redirecting corporate subsidies (not modelled).

plans.label: Operation Double Nickel
plans.description: Lt. Gov. Patrick's plan (Dec 2025): the school homestead exemption rises from $140,000 to $180,000, and the senior school exemption and tax freeze start at 55 instead of 65 (so owners 55+ get $240,000). The state pays districts back. No bill yet.

plans.label: Republican Party of Texas platform
plans.description: 2026 platform planks 79-80: values rolled back to 2019 and then capped at 3% a year for all property (cost basis), school homestead exemptions applied at every taxing unit, no local rate increases without a two-thirds vote (modelled as none passing), spending limits for all units, and all property taxes eliminated over five years (paid by the state; the platform rules out an income tax). The surplus buy-down and bond rules are separate settings.

knobs.label: Surplus spent on school buy-downs a year

plans.label: Texas Democratic Party platform
plans.description: 2026-28 platform: a temporary freeze on residential appraisals (here 2027-2028) and a flat-dollar homestead exemption at every county, city and district (here $25,000; the platform names no amount), with the cost shifted to other property when units keep their revenue. Renters' exemptions, sale-price disclosure, current-use valuation and data center rules are not modelled.
